title: The going turns bad
text: The road gives out into churned mud and deadfall. There is a longer way round on firmer ground, and there is straight through.

choices.label: Let the scout find a line
Go round by the long way

then.text: The long way is dry and certain, and it takes exactly as long as it looks.

pass.text: %s breaks a path and the rest follow in the ruts. They come out the far side ahead of the day.

fail.text: The mud wins. Boots lost, ankles turned, and most of the day with them.

title: Tracks across the road
text: Fresh prints cross the road and go off into the scrub — a good many feet, not all of them in boots.

pass.text: %s keeps the trail through the scrub. Smoke, ahead, low down.

fail.text: The trail goes to stone and stops. An afternoon spent learning nothing.

then.text: Whoever it was, they are going somewhere else. The company lets them.

title: Smoke in a hollow
text: A cookfire in a hollow off the trail, and the ones who made the tracks around it. They have not seen the company yet.

then.text: No time to count them. The company goes in.

pass.text: %s lies in the bracken until dark and comes back with where they sleep and where they came from.

fail.text: A dry stick, a shout, and the hollow empties toward the company.

then.text: The company goes back the way it came and leaves the fire to them.

title: Someone on the road
text: A lone traveller, hood up, walking the other way. They slow when they see the company.

choices.label: Pay them to show you a way

then.text: Twenty coins and a scratched map on the back of a bill. There is a way the company did not know.

pass.text: %s gets it out of them: a path off the road nobody marks. The company will know it when they pass it.

fail.text: They say the road is the road and keep walking.

title: Something half-buried
text: The corner of a strongbox shows through the leaf mould under a split oak.

pass.text: %s has it up in an hour. Somebody's savings, and they are not coming back for them.

fail.text: An hour of digging for a box of rust and wet paper.

then.text: The company covers it back over. Word of that kind of thing gets round the villages.

title: The stream runs wrong
text: The only water for miles has a sheen on it and a smell under that.

then.text: Slow, smoky and safe. Nobody gets sick; everybody gets tired of waiting.

choices.label: Go thirsty to the next spring

pass.text: %s knows where the next clean spring will be, and it is there.

fail.text: The next spring is further than anyone guessed. They reach it grey and stumbling.

title: Clear running
text: Firm ground, a dry sky, and a road that goes where it says it does.

then.text: An hour in the sun with boots off. It is worth more than the hour.

title: The ford runs high
text: Brown water, running fast and loud, over a ford that was knee-deep the last time anyone crossed it.

choices.label: Let the scout find the bar
Wait for the water to drop

then.text: By evening it is back to knee-deep. By evening.

pass.text: %s takes the rope over first and anchors it. Everyone crosses wet and whole.

fail.text: The rope holds; a pack does not.

title: A pole across the road
text: Six of them and a pole across the road. They call it a toll. It is not a toll.

then.text: The pole goes up. Nobody on either side pretends it was a toll.
The company does not pay people for standing in a road.

title: A shrine at the crossroads
text: A stone niche at the crossroads, old flowers in it, and a bowl for whatever passers-by can spare.

then.text: Coin in the bowl and a quiet minute. The company leaves lighter in more ways than one.
The company has somewhere to be.

title: A waystone in the grass
text: A standing stone half-sunk in the grass, cut with marks older than any road the company knows.

choices.label: Let the scout make it out

pass.text: %s works out what it pointed at: a way the old road took that nobody walks now. It will show itself to anyone who knows to look.

fail.text: An hour with charcoal and paper, and the marks make no more sense on the page.

then.text: It has stood this long without the company's help.

title: Wire across the path
text: Snare wire at ankle height, across the path and into the brush. Somebody out here is hunting more than deer.

pass.text: %s follows the wire back to where it is tied off, and the hide beside it.

fail.text: The wire runs everywhere and nowhere. An hour lost among it.

choices.label: Cut the wire and move on

then.text: Whoever set it can set it again somewhere else.

title: A hide in the brush
text: A hide of woven branches, a man in it with a knife and a great many skins, and very little interest in visitors.

then.text: He sells a draught he swears by and wants them gone before he changes his mind.

pass.text: %s talks dogs with him until he talks paths. There is one the company did not know.

fail.text: He points at the road and says nothing else.

pass.text: %s makes it plain. He packs his skins before they are out of sight.

fail.text: He is not alone out here, and his friends take it badly.

title: What is left of a company
text: A burned wagon, the bones of the team, and what is left of the people who were driving it.

choices.label: Go over it for anything useful

then.text: Shallow graves and their names where the names could be found. It costs the afternoon.

pass.text: %s finds where they came from and where they went back to.

fail.text: The trail finds the company first.

title: The sky goes the wrong colour
text: The light goes green over the hills and the birds stop. Something is coming across the country fast.

then.text: Cloaks over heads in a ditch while it goes over. Wet, cold, and whole.

pass.text: %s picks the ridge out of the murk and they are under the overhang before the worst of it.

fail.text: Caught halfway up the slope in the open, and it is every bit as bad as it looked.

title: A wheel in the ditch
text: A carter with his wheel in the ditch, his team straining, and his load going nowhere.

then.text: Slower than the company would walk, but he talks the whole way, and every word of it is about them by the time he gets there.
Somebody else will be along.

title: Families on the road with what they could carry.
text: Carts, children, a cow on a rope. They are walking away from something, and they keep looking back.

then.text: It is not much, and it is noticed. Word of it will reach the town they came from.

pass.text: %s keeps them moving and keeps an eye behind. On the way the grandmother tells them exactly where the raiders came from.

fail.text: They are followed. Whoever drove them out is not finished with them.
